title: Rotary Airlock Feeder

introduction.definition: A rotary airlock (rotary valve) feeder has a rotor with pockets turning in a close-fitting housing. Powder enters the top pockets, is carried round and drops out at the bottom. Because the vane tips seal against the housing, it meters the solids while limiting air leakage between two zones at different pressure — for example a hopper and a pneumatic conveying line.
applications: Metering powders from silos (cement, flour, plastics, fly ash)
key_points: Volumetric — rate ∝ rotor speed × pocket volume × fill
Seals pressure difference by tight tip clearance
Leakage air rises with clearance and ΔP
Speed kept moderate so pockets fill
introduction.summary: A rotary airlock feeder (rotary valve) meters powder or granules from a hopper into a pneumatic conveying line or out of a cyclone/filter while sealing the pressure difference. A vaned rotor turns in a close-fitting housing; each pocket fills at the top and empties at the bottom.

foundation: Support on steelwork or a concrete plinth designed for the hopper/bin load on the feeder plus impact and dynamic loads.
Isolate vibrating machines from the structure with their springs/rubber mounts — never weld or rigidly bolt the vibrating body to the structure.
alignment: Set the feeder at the designed slope and centre it under the hopper outlet; set skirt boards and the hopper gate to the design bed depth.
Align drive and driven shafts (laser or dial gauge) or set the exciter motors as the maker specifies.
piping: Fit a vent on the inlet side of airlocks feeding pressure lines so leakage air does not fluidise or block the incoming powder.
Bolt flanges without distorting the housing (clearances are small).
commissioning: Run empty first: check direction, amplitude/speed, temperatures and noise.
Load gradually, check the material bed is even and the discharge rate matches the set-point; record motor current as a baseline.

routine.task: Watch for falling throughput, noise and leakage.

periodic.task: Check tip/side clearances with feeler gauges.

overhaul.task: Rebuild rotor (re-tip) and housing; replace shaft seals and bearings.

lubrication: Drive gearbox and chain: oil/grease to schedule; end-plate bearings greased.

symptoms: Reduced capacity, powder bridging above valve
remedies: Restore clearances; fit vent; consider adjustable tips

causes: Foreign object, thermal expansion with hot product

safety: Never put fingers in the inlet or outlet — the rotor shears like a guillotine. Lock out before inspection.
Use certified flameproof designs for combustible dust zones.

video_tutorials.title: Rotary Airlock Feeder — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Rotary Airlock Feeder.
A rotary airlock (rotary valve) feeder has a rotor with pockets turning in a close-fitting housing.
Powder enters the top pockets, is carried round and drops out at the bottom.
Because the vane tips seal against the housing, it meters the solids while limiting air leakage between two zones at different pressure — for example a hopper and a pneumatic conveying line.

Typical applications include feeding pneumatic conveying lines; discharging dust collectors and cyclones; metering powders from silos (cement, flour, plastics, fly ash); explosion isolation (certified designs).

The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Housing (inlet top, outlet bottom; close rotor clearance), Rotor (8 vanes, closed end discs) & Shaft, End Cover with Bearing & Shaft Seal (hidden in cutaway).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Rotary Airlock Feeder — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Rotary Airlock Feeder.
Watch for falling throughput, noise and leakage.
Check tip/side clearances with feeler gauges.
Rebuild rotor (re-tip) and housing; replace shaft seals and bearings.
Watch for excessive air leakage: reduced capacity, powder bridging above valve. Common cause: worn tips/housing.
Watch for rotor jam: motor trip, shear pin broken. Common cause: foreign object, thermal expansion with hot product.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
